description: Signed x * 3 / 2 without overflow (nsw mul) not rewritten to a cheaper form
notes: C taken from the issue's src2 reproducer (signed version; the unsigned version is already optimized); clang produces the issue's IR: mul nsw + sdiv. The issue's target x + x / 2 saves an instruction on AArch64 and RISC-V but not on x86: godbolt llc trunk (-mcpu=skylake) gives 5 instructions plus ret for both, and llvm-mca trunk gives 190 vs 187 cycles per 100 iterations. expected.ll uses a variant of the same idea that is shorter on x86: since 3x does not overflow, 3x and x have the same sign, so the rounding bias of the signed division can be taken from x: (3x + (x >>u 31)) >>s 1, 4 instructions plus ret, 161 cycles in llvm-mca. The issue's own target is also proven correct by Alive2 against this source. expected.ll proven correct (refinement) by Alive2 alive-tv, 2026-10-28: src = clang trunk -O3 IR of src.c (godbolt cclang_trunk, -O3 --target=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -march=skylake -emit-llvm -S -g0) renamed @src, tgt = expected.ll renamed @tgt, identical signature; output 'Transformation seems to be correct!' with no warning. Run on Alive2's own Compiler Explorer instance (alive2.llvm.org/ce, compiler id 'alive'), since godbolt.org does not host alive-tv.
